subject: EU finance dataset — PII handling matrix and regional routing exception
messages:
From: Maria Rossi <maria.rossi@acme-finance.eu>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy@acme-finance.eu
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: PII handling matrix / routing exception for EU finance dataset

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. We're in the final stages of our DPA review and have one outstanding operational clarification for the EU production finance dataset (dataset id: eufinance-prod-transaction-logs). Two short asks:

1) We need confirmation that any PII (full identifiers, payment instrument hashes linked to customer IDs) originating from EU residents is not routed outside EU regions except under a documented customer instruction. If there are any background flows (analytics, ML training, telemetry) to non-EU regions, please list and justify.

2) Please provide an updated PII handling matrix and the regional data flow diagram showing where KMS keys are held and which subprocessors have access to decrypted material.

We attach the DPA redlines (see note below) and would appreciate a short attestation we can include with our procurement file while legal finishes the annex.

--Attachment: Acme_DPA_Redlines_20270622.pdf (pdf)--

Thanks,
Maria Rossi
Head of Data Privacy, Acme Finance
privacy@acme-finance.eu

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Maria Rossi <maria.rossi@acme-finance.eu>
Cc: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: PII handling matrix / routing exception for EU finance dataset

Maria — thanks for the clear asks. High level answers first, then attachments and next steps.

Short answers:
- EU-origin PII is served and stored in EU regions by default; we do not route primary production traffic to non-EU regions unless a customer explicitly opts into cross-region replication for DR/workloads.
- Background analytics and model training use pseudonymized aggregates derived from tokenized identifiers; raw identifiers are excluded from training pipelines unless explicitly included by the customer and executed in a pinned region.
- KMS keys for Acme Finance (customer-managed option selected) are provisioned in the EU and keys are under your KMS. For Redwood-managed keys, the primary key is EU-resident and backups replicate within EU zones only.
- Current subprocessors with potential access in EU flows: cloud-provider-eu (compute), observability-eu (logs aggregator, only pseudonymized logs), and a managed-uploads vendor (EU-only). Full list attached.

Attachments included: 20270622_pii_handling_matrix.xlsx (matrix with field-level mapping, retention, pseudonymization status) and regional_dataflow_eu.svg (diagram showing primary flow + KMS).

Quick clarifications we still need from you to finalize the matrix: which retention class should apply to the raw transaction identifiers (you listed both "sensitive" and "analytics-transient" in your redlines) and whether you require us to sign an annex that prevents cross-region failover.

Can we schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk the diagram? I can loop in PrIyom for the KMS/crypto specifics and Hannah for legal evidence.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Privacy Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
--Attachment: 20270622_pii_handling_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)--
--Attachment: regional_dataflow_eu.svg (image)--

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:10:00 +0200
Subject: Re: PII handling matrix / routing exception for EU finance dataset

Jonas — quick internal notes to finalize the deliverable before the call:

- Retention: recommend defaulting raw identifiers to "sensitive - 30d" unless Acme confirms a longer business requirement. Put an option for "analytics-transient" where tokenization is applied and original data is deleted within 7 days.
- Evidence: we should prepare a single ZIP with (a) KMS key metadata (key-id + region + rotation policy), (b) hardened network diagram callouts, (c) subprocessors CSV and (d) a 1-page attestation for Acme to attach to their procurement packet.
- Subprocessor nuance: managed-uploads vendor only processes encrypted blobs server-side in EU and never has plaintext access. Observability vendor receives pseudonymized traces; we should add a note about sampling and redaction.

I'll draft the attestation text and populate HubSpot ticket RED-8321 with the artifacts link: https://hub.redwood.com/ticket/RED-8321.

—PrIyom
Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: Maria Rossi <maria.rossi@acme-finance.eu>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy@acme-finance.eu
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:45:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: PII handling matrix / routing exception for EU finance dataset

Thanks Jonas — the docs look good at first pass. A couple follow-up points before the call:

- Confirm dataset id: eufinance-prod-transaction-logs is covered by the same region routing controls (yes/no).
- For the KMS backups, can you confirm the geographic scope of the backups and the roles that can request key export? We need a one-line statement we can include in our procurement risk register (who can export, where exports are allowed).
- We also need a short attestation statement that Redwood will not use raw EU-origin PII for model training without explicit customer consent.

If you can push a short attestation and the KMS metadata before 11:00 CET we'll attach them to our packet and likely clear procurement signoff today.

Regards,
Maria

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Maria Rossi <maria.rossi@acme-finance.eu>
Cc: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 12:05:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: PII handling matrix / routing exception for EU finance dataset

Maria — quick summary and attestation for your procurement packet (see attached evidence ZIP).

Attestation (for Acme Finance procurement file):
- Redwood Inference confirms that EU-origin primary production traffic for dataset id eufinance-prod-transaction-logs is held and processed in EU regions by default and will not be routed outside the EU without an explicit, documented instruction from Acme Finance.
- Redwood will not use raw, identifiable EU-origin PII for model training, or telemetry-derived training datasets, without explicit written consent from Acme Finance.
- KMS posture: primary keys for Acme Finance are provisioned in EU (eu-central-1) for both Redwood-managed and customer-managed options. Key export is only permitted to a customer-managed KMS under the customer account; Redwood personnel do not have key export rights. Backup replication is limited to EU zones.

Next steps (action items):
1) PrIyom to upload evidence ZIP to HubSpot ticket RED-8321 and share Drive link (done).
2) Jonas to schedule 30-min technical sync for Thursday 10:00 CET (invite sent).
3) Hannah to confirm DPA annex language for the cross-region failover clause by end of day.

Attachments: eufinance-evidence-pack.zip (contains KMS metadata, subprocessors.csv, hardened network diagram, 1-page attestation PDF).

Thanks — please reply if you need additional wording.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Privacy Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
--Attachment: eufinance-evidence-pack.zip (zip)--
